note: The audit for tools/lint-event-derived-id-minting.py. One entry per file that mints an id for a kind whose id MUST come from its create Event (zh/models/common-fields.md section 6.0). `verdict` is what the site should be, not permission to stay: `event_derived` and `local_ref` entries are open defects. Cross-repo: `repo` is the checkout directory name.

entries.reason: The five retained generators for event-derived kinds (realm, space, event, relation, circle) plus `generate_view_id`, and the unit tests that exercise them. The file documents them as known defects with `Do not add callers`; the SDK debug_assert panics on each, which is what the remaining ids.rs test failures report. Removing them is the outcome of the soland local-projection decision in arkret-work/work/active/2026-08-06-event-derived-id-handover.md section 3.
Mints a Realm id on the admin collection surface. Handover section 3 site 1 of 5.

`body.realm_id.unwrap_or_else(ids::generate_realm_id)` — a sovereign Realm create falls back to a minted id when the caller omits one. Handover section 3 site 2 of 5. Found only after the scanner learned the bare function-reference form: with `--root` alone it is invisible to a `generate_realm_id(` grep.
Mints a Circle id. Handover section 3 site 3 of 5.
Mints an Event id during Applet install. Handover section 3 site 4 of 5.

Mints circle + strand + relation + two Event ids for one object graph. Handover section 3 site 5 of 5, and the one that additionally needs the attach Event's prev_refs reordered into build-then-derive.
`authorized_event_ref` names a device-authorization Event that was never authored; the in-file comment already states the fix is to author it. Not in the handover's list of five.
A contact-managed consent grant mints the `ak:event:` value its cell dot is built from; the in-file comment already states the fix is to author the Event. Not in the handover's list of five.
MIMI room-binding emits a projection row keyed by a minted `ak:event:`; the in-file comment already states the fix is to author the Event. Not in the handover's list of five.

The MIMI facade notify record is broadcast and deliberately not persisted into durable history, so it stands behind no Event at all: it wants `ak:local_ref:`, not a fabricated Event id. Not in the handover's list of five.

`OrganizationRecord.source_refs` on a locally synthesized record points at a minted Event id. The record is server-local provenance, so the reference belongs to `ak:local_ref:` (or should be absent) rather than claiming an Event.

Same shape as organizations.rs for a synthesized Realm record's `source_refs` (line ~157, production). The same file's `accepted_event_command_is_committed_through_one_port` test also mints ids, which is fixture use.
Synthetic Event and Realm ids for Events that exist only in this test's store.
Synthetic Event id for a fixture Event.
Store-contract fixtures need distinct ids per row; no Event is authored.
Storage contract tests mint Realm and Event ids for rows they insert directly.

The create-channel surface picks the `ak:strand:` id client-side and passes it to `discussion_strand_create`, so the object's identity is producer-chosen. The strand id must be `retype(create.event_id)`.
Board Space, list Space and strand ids are all minted client-side before the create Events are built. Same fix as chat/mod.rs.

`new_chat_message_id` mints an optimistic-UI id and it is also stored as `ChatMessage.protocol_message_id`, so a local placeholder is presented as a protocol id. The local handle needs its own local kind; the protocol id may only be filled in once the create Event exists.
Inside `live_owner_kanban_writes_against_dev_soland`, a dev-only probe against a local soland.
The grant / revoke fanout payloads carry a minted `ak:event:` for an Event coauth never authors. Either the Event is authored (and its id derived) or the field must name a local reference.
Test row builder for an `authorized_event` payload.
`create_portal_strand` mints the portal `ak:strand:` id before building `StrandCreateObject`, so the bridge names the strand instead of deriving it from the create Event it is about to submit.
Wire-probe CLI: prints a synthetic bootstrap create Event id for manual inspection.
Synthetic authorize Event id in an e2e fixture.
Synthetic Event ids in a device-enrolment rollout fixture.
